chunks: And Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from Yahya ibn al-Mubarik, from Abdullah ibn Jabala, from Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Sayrafi, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding the saying of Allah, Exalted and Mighty: 'So whoever hastens [his departure] within two days - there is no blame upon him' ... 'for whoever feared' the game, meaning during his ihram. 'If he catches it, he is not permitted to depart in the first departure.'
And it is upon the Imam to depart before midday in the final departure, so that he may pray Dhuhr in Mecca. Narrated.

key_terms.إِحْرَامٌ: The state of ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah
key_terms.الزَّوَالُ: Midday, when the sun begins to decline from its zenith

ai.seo_question: What are the rules for departing Mina and praying Dhuhr during Hajj if game is caught?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* elucidates the jurisprudential distinction between the voluntary early departure and the mandatory final departure from Mina, emphasizing the Imam's role in synchronizing the community's exit with the Dhuhr prayer in Mecca. It highlights the Shia scholarly focus on the practical application of Quranic verses regarding the days of Tashriq, ensuring that the ritual of leaving Mina aligns with the prescribed timing for congregational prayer.
